s1.quote: Nine Mile Reef … grey nurse sharks in winter. … The top of the reef sits at about 10 metres deep, dropping to 30 metres

s2.quote: Nine Mile Reef varies in depth from 12m to 30m … the reef often has strong currents, sometimes ripping by at three knots

s3.quote: Nine Mile Reef is located off the Tweed Coast and an advanced dive. Due to the presence of current most of the time, the dive is often a drift dive

highlights.text: Grey nurse sharks in winter, leopard sharks in summer
Wobbegongs year-round; bull sharks drop in

hazards.text: Strong current, up to about three knots
Often a drift dive with blue-water safety stops

summary.text: An offshore reef off Tweed Heads with a rocky ridge, ledges and bommies from about 10 m to 30 m. It is a shark site, with grey nurse sharks in winter and wobbegongs all year, but strong current and the need for calm seas make it for experienced divers.

s1.quote: Navigating Twin Peaks can challenge some novice divers, so a Dive Guide is recommended. The Reef wall, just 15 metres southeast of the peaks, offers a beautiful sandy slope

highlights.text: Two coral-covered peaks with a sandy reef wall nearby

hazards.text: Navigation can challenge novices; guide recommended

s1.quote: Turtle Bommie A large bommie structure surrounded by beautiful hard and soft corals … The white sandy bottom makes it easy to navigate … This site is a must for a night dive

highlights.text: Turtles sleeping on reef shelves; good night dive
Large bommie ringed by hard and soft corals

s1.quote: Alma Bay … The bay has a rocky headland above each end of the beach, which deepens along a gentle gradient to about 5m to 6m at the mouth of the bay.

s2.quote: With depths of just 5 to 8 meters, Alma Bay is perfect for beginners

highlights.text: Granite boulders, corals, rays and nudibranchs
Green turtles cruise through

summary.text: A sheltered, patrolled beach on Magnetic Island that slopes gently to about 5-8 m, used heavily for teaching new divers. Granite boulders, corals, rays, nudibranchs and the odd turtle make it a relaxed shore dive.

s1.quote: Popes Eye is a popular short-stay destination for pleasure craft and Licensed Tour Operators. There is good snorkelling within the structure, but more experience is necessary when diving on the outside of it.

s2.quote: Popes Eye 0-12m … Pope's Eye is a man made basalt rock annulus … The inside of Pope's Eye provides a safe anchorage in 2 meters of water

access.value: Port Phillip Heads Marine National Park; boat access

highlights.text: Snorkel and shallow dive inside the ring
Australasian gannet colony on the rock

hazards.text: Outside wall needs more diving experience

summary.text: A man-made basalt ring in the Port Phillip Heads Marine National Park with a sheltered, 2 m deep centre and a wall dropping to about 12 m outside. The inside suits snorkellers and new divers, while the outside needs more experience.

s1.quote: Portsea Hole is one of the most popular recreational dives sites for experienced divers, reaching depths of up to 30m. Experienced divers can explore the spectacular vertical reef

highlights.text: Vertical reef with sponges, soft corals and invertebrates

access.value: Inside Port Phillip Heads Marine National Park

s1.quote: Boarfish Reef: Boarfish is an extension of Lonsdale Wall and ranges from 10m-25m depth, meandering over drop-offs through caves, overhangs and swim-throughs.

s2.quote: Boarfish Reef 8-22m … The reef, which lies approximately halfway between Queenscliff and Point Lonsdale starts in approx. 10m of water and drops off to 22m

highlights.text: Caves, overhangs and swim-throughs
Blue devilfish, crayfish and boarfish

summary.text: A colourful reef between Queenscliff and Point Lonsdale, an extension of the Lonsdale Wall. It runs from about 10 m down to 22-25 m over drop-offs, caves and swim-throughs, with blue devilfish, crayfish and boarfish.

s1.quote: The Grotto (12-22m)
Lonsdale Wall: A picture perfect slack water site ranging from 12m-38m, Lonsdale Wall features huge overhangs, undercuts and ledges

s2.quote: Lonsdale Wall can refer to the entire wall system or a specific site (max 38m) on the wall.

highlights.text: Overhangs and ledges covered in zoanthids and sponges

hazards.text: Best at slack water or as a drift dive

s1.quote: J4 Submarine (max 28m) – A WW1 submarine. Usually an easy dive, but can be susceptible to surge.
Lonsdale Bommies 12-20m
Castle Rock (max 20m) – An easy dive, a large bommie showcasing a temperate reef.

highlights.text: Large bommie with temperate reef life

s1.quote: Rye Pier: Recent reconstruction makes the long walk from the carpark to the purpose-built diver’s platform even smoother. Large stingrays and seahorses are commonly sighted

highlights.text: Large stingrays and seahorses

access.value: Long walk from car park to purpose-built diver platform

s1.quote: Blairegowrie Pier (max 7m) – An easy dive, great for night dives and macro life. A popular spot to see spider crab migrations. Blairegowrie Pier is an active boat pier, so divers need to be aware of No Go Zones.

s2.quote: Blairgowrie Pier: Blairgowrie’s purpose-built dive platform is the gateway to some of the state’s shallowest but richest artificial marine life environments.

highlights.text: Macro life and nudibranchs under the pier
Spider crab aggregations

hazards.text: Active boat pier with no-go zones

summary.text: A very shallow pier dive from a purpose-built platform, rich in macro life under the pylons. It can be dived day or night, and spider crabs gather at times. Stay out of the boat no-go zones.

s1.quote: You can only dive “comfortably” under the bridge on still water at high or low tide. … We set you up with the gear and jump in across the road at the boat ramp entry point.

hazards.text: Strong tidal flow; dive only on still water

s1.quote: Flagstaff … You can enter from the sandy beach at the bay … It's a shallow dive ranging in depth from 5 metres to 8 metres, Flagstaff suits all ranges of diver skills.

highlights.text: Grey nurse sharks visit in winter
Rays on sand, nudibranchs in weed gardens

s1.quote: The old coal loader is the dominating feature of the bay, a shallow dive that goes to about 11m. … ship chains, cables and hardware including the remains of the SS Wallarah.

highlights.text: Pylons grown into a reef with fish and nudibranchs
Ship chains and remains of the SS Wallarah

sites.name: Moon Island

s1.publisher: Michael McFadyen's Scuba Diving Web Site
s1.quote: The Arch is south-east of the island … The depth just off these boulders is about 20 metres

s2.quote: between Flagstaff and Moon Island we are lucky enough to get visits from the Grey Nurse Sharks

highlights.text: Grey nurse shark visits in winter
The Arch: large boulders with an archway

sites.depthNote: The Arch off the south-east side: archway about 17 m, sand about 20 m

s1.quote: Bare Island La Perouse, NSW … Depth 3–12m … Bare Island Left is the eastern side, entered off the eastern face of the South-Eastern Point. … Currents are generally weak

s2.quote: Left Side … which is the best side, but a bit tricky in even a mild southerly swell … The max depth is about 12m

s3.quote: NSW National Parks and Wildlife Service has closed the whole Bare Island precinct … from 24 August 2026 while the 1887 bridge is restored. Reopening is expected in late 2027

access.value: Bare Island precinct closed for bridge restoration from 24 Aug 2026; reopening expected late 2027

hazards.text: Surge around the point; tricky in southerly swell

summary.text: The eastern face of Bare Island in Botany Bay, entered from the south-east point and slippery to exit, so it suits divers who know the site. Max depth is about 12 m with soft corals and macro life; southerly swell makes it tricky. The precinct is currently closed.

s1.quote: Bare Island Right is the western side. Divers enter at the Western Point in calm seas … That boat ramp is the standard exit for every dive on the western side … an easy entry for beginners.

s2.quote: Right Side, which is where you dive when there's a mild Southerly swell … The max depth is about 12m

s3.quote: NSW National Parks and Wildlife Service has closed the whole Bare Island precinct … from 24 August 2026 while the 1887 bridge is restored. Reopening is expected in late 2027

access.value: Bare Island precinct closed for bridge restoration from 24 Aug 2026; reopening expected late 2027

highlights.text: Sheltered side, dived in southerly swell

summary.text: The western, sheltered side of Bare Island in Botany Bay, with an easy entry and a boat-ramp exit that suit beginners. Depths reach about 12 m, and it is the side to choose when southerly swell is running. The precinct is currently closed.
